channel.title: Hyndburn Council Transparency — AI DOGE
channel.description: Independent analysis of Hyndburn Borough Council spending and governance.

item.title: Worldpay: Why Does Hyndburn Pay 80x More Than Blackburn?
item.description: Hyndburn pays £1,900 average per Worldpay transaction vs £24 at neighbouring Blackburn — a 7,970% price gap for the same payment processing service. Different service tier, different contract terms, or a bad deal?

item.title: AJ Developments: £40K to a Company Facing Strike-Off
item.description: AJ Developments (NW) Ltd received £39.8K from Hyndburn while facing Companies House strike-off proceedings with an overdue confirmation statement. If struck off, the council loses contractual recourse for defective work.

item.title: 2,422 Transactions at £5 Each: Hyndburn's Land Registry Habit
item.description: Hyndburn made 2,422 individual £5 Land Registry searches totalling £12K. Legitimate property checks, but at scale this suggests the council lacks a bulk search arrangement. Consolidation could save admin time and cost.

item.title: The Barnfield Question: Does Hyndburn Have a JV Too?
item.description: Burnley's Barnfield JV spans 5 councils (£38.8M combined). Pendle has PEARL. Rossendale has RTB. At Burnley, the Council Leader is JV co-director. Does Hyndburn have a Barnfield entity in its supply chain, and if so, who governs it?

item.title: Specialist Fleet Services: £1.87M with No Companies House Record
item.description: Specialist Fleet Services received £1.87M from Hyndburn with no Companies House registration, scoring 40/100 on the supplier risk index. Along with Autotech Recruit (£131K) and DVLA (£22K), three elevated-risk suppliers operate without standard corporate governance verification.

item.title: No Directors, No Problem? £1.1M to Companies Without Governance
item.description: B3P Services (£420K), JDS Trucks (£287K), and Homewise Society (£159K) received £866K from Hyndburn with no active directors registered at Companies House. 17 suppliers in total received £1.1M while in breach of the Companies Act 2006.

item.title: 12.9x Year-End Spike: Hyndburn's Regeneration Rush
item.description: Hyndburn's Regeneration & Housing department spent 12.9x its monthly average in March — the highest year-end spike of any Lancashire election council. £3.7M above normal was pushed through in a single month. While overall March spending is the lowest month, this department bucks the trend dramatically.

item.title: 670 Split Payment Instances: The £14.8M Question
item.description: 670 instances of payments to the same supplier within short windows that individually fall below approval thresholds. £14.8M in suspected split payments. Are these genuine operational costs or deliberate threshold avoidance? Hyndburn's low £250 threshold makes this the most granular split-payment analysis of any Lancashire council.
